title: Storage Queues
description: Use Azure Storage Queues to decouple application components and build resilient message-based workflows.

data.text: Azure Queue Storage is a simple, cost-effective service for storing large numbers of messages. A **queue** decouples different parts of an application so they can communicate reliably even when one side is temporarily unavailable. A producer sends messages, and a consumer picks them up and processes them.

data.title: Common Patterns
items: **Background work** — offload slow tasks like image resizing so the web app can respond quickly.
**Work distribution** — spread work across multiple worker instances for scale.
**Resilience** — buffer requests during spikes so the backend is not overwhelmed.
**Decoupling** — let the API and background worker evolve independently.

data.title: Send a Message with Azure CLI
data.content: Add a message to a storage queue
data.code:
az storage message put \
  --account-name stdemostorage \
  --queue-name work-items \
  --content '{"task":"resize-image","id":101}' \
  --time-to-live 3600

data.content: Receive and delete a message from a queue

terms.definition: A FIFO (first-in, first-out) message store that buffers work between application components.
A text payload up to 64 KB stored in a queue, typically JSON describing a unit of work.
The time a received message is hidden from other consumers while being processed.
A message that repeatedly fails processing and should be moved to a dead-letter queue.

data.title: At-Least-Once Delivery
data.text: Storage Queues deliver each message at least once. Your consumer must be idempotent: processing the same message twice should not corrupt data or create duplicate work.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Producer and Consumer
data.description: Create a simple app that sends and receives messages from a storage queue.
steps: Create a storage queue named 'work-items' using Azure CLI.
Write a small app that sends 5 JSON messages to the queue.
Write a second app that receives one message at a time and prints it.
Add error handling so failed messages are logged instead of crashing the consumer.
data.expectedOutcome: Two working apps that communicate through an Azure Storage Queue.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Storage Queues decouple producers from consumers reliably.
Messages are text-based and up to 64 KB.
Visibility timeout prevents multiple consumers from processing the same message.
Design consumers to be idempotent because delivery is at-least-once.
data.takeaway: Queues are a simple but powerful tool for building resilient, distributed applications on Azure.
